The '''Motherlode Mine''' is a [[Members-only]] low-intensity [[Mining]] training area located in the [[Dwarven Mine]]. No level is required to access it, but 30 Mining (not boostable) is required to mine in the area. The activity involves mining [[ore vein]]s for [[pay dirt]], depositing the pay dirt into a [[hopper (Motherlode Mine)|hopper]] to clean it, then collecting cleaned ores as well as [[golden nuggets]] from the [[Sack (Motherlode Mine)|sack]] after a short delay.

The mine consists of two levels, with the upper level requiring 57 Mining (not boostable) and a one time payment of 100 golden nuggets to access. The hopper on this level also requires an additional 50 nuggets to use.

[[Golden nuggets]] can also be exchanged for a variety of [[Motherlode Mine#Rewards|other rewards]] from [[Prospector Percy]], including the [[Prospector set]], [[gem bag]] and [[coal bag]].

==Transportation==
There are several ways to access the mine. It is strongly recommended to bring a [[pickaxe]] to enter the mine and for further passage, as opposed to relying on other players and [[Miner (Motherlode Mine)|miners]] to remove the [[rockfall]]s that block the area.

* The quickest way to reach the mine is to teleport outside the gate leading to the [[Mining Guild]] with a [[Skills necklace]], which will put you just south-west of the mine entrance. 60 Mining is '''not''' required to enter with this method.
*Players can also enter the Dwarven Mine via the house in north-eastern [[Falador]], east of the [[Falador Party Room]]. Taking the stairs will put players just north of a cave entrance to the mine.
*Players with 60 Mining can enter the Mining Guild directly and run east until they see a cave entrance.
*Finally, players can enter the Dwarven Mine via the camp south of [[Ice Mountain]], and walk south-east to the northern entrance.

==Mechanics==
{{Clear|left}}

===Mining ore veins===
[[File:Motherlode Mine - Mining ore veins.png|thumb|Mining ore veins]]
[[Ore vein]]s are scattered throughout both levels of the mine, and may be mined with any [[pickaxe]] yielding 60 Mining [[experience]] each. After the first [[pay-dirt]] has been mined by '''any''' player, a 23-27 second timer will start, after which the vein will be depleted. This timer is increased to 36-40 on the upper level. The double ore bonus of the [[Varrock armour]] does '''not''' affect pay-dirt.

The veins also have a chance to give [[uncut gem]]s for no experience. Wearing an [[amulet of glory]] will increase the chance of giving an [[uncut gem]]. As each gem mined decreases the experience rate per inventory, this is not recommended if looking to maximise experience rates. If you wish to keep the gems, you may consider using a [[gem bag]] to store them.

[[Clue geode]]s cannot be obtained from ore veins.

{{Skilling success chart|label=Pay-dirt mining chance|showbefore=no|xlabel=Mining Level
|label1=Pay-dirt|low1=60|high1=105|req1=30|color1=brown|image1=Pay-dirt.png
}}

===Mine layout===
Rocks fall on certain tiles around the mine; these [[rockfall]]s block access to veins or other areas of the mine, and will deal 1-4 damage to any players on the tile. Removing them requires a pickaxe and rewards 10 Mining experience each. [[Runite Minor]] and the other [[Miner (Motherlode Mine)|miner]]s may occasionally remove these rockfalls, though they usually just mine pay-dirt. [[Box trap]]s and other traps placed on the ground may be laid to temporarily prevent rockfalls from blocking a path, until the trap collapses.

Near [[Prospector Percy]] is a bank chest that can be accessed without any requirements, though this cannot be used to bank pay-dirt (see the cleaning pay-dirt section below). There is also a [[Dark tunnel (Motherlode Mine)|dark tunnel]] next to it, an [[Agility]] [[shortcut]] (requires 54 Agility and completion of the medium [[Falador Diary]]) that connects the east side of the mine to the centre. There is a similar tunnel to the south which does not require diary completion.

====Upper level====
Unlocking the upper level of the mine requires base 57 [[Mining]], and a one-time fee of 100 [[golden nugget]]s paid to [[Prospector Percy]]. It can be accessed from a [[Ladder (Motherlode Mine)|ladder]] north of the bank chest.

The upper level consists of 64 ore veins clustered closer together than on the lower level. These ore veins deplete at a much slower rate, depleting after 36-40 seconds instead of the usual 23-27 seconds.

===Cleaning pay-dirt===
Pay-dirt cannot be banked (though it can be dropped), and may be cleaned in order to gain bonus experience and collect various ores and [[golden nuggets]].

Cleaning pay-dirt involves depositing it into a [[Hopper (Motherlode Mine)|hopper]]. A hopper can be found on each level, both easily accessible from the upper level. The hopper on the upper level is much closer to the ore veins, and allows players to deposit pay-dirt without needing to use the ladder to return to the lower level. The player must unlock this hopper with 50 golden nuggets by speaking to Prospector Percy, while the hopper on the lower level is free.

Once deposited, pay-dirt will make its way towards the [[Sack (Motherlode Mine)|sack]] to the south, taking 8 seconds, at which point players will receive bonus experience. This process requires the water to be flowing (see the Water circuit section below). The sack can then be searched to collect various ores and [[golden nuggets]]. Bonus experience will increase with higher mining levels, as higher-tier ores are cleaned. The average bonus experience per pay dirt cleaned varies with Mining level; being 16.84 at level 85 and 21.9 at level 99. 

Each ore has a level requirement equal to the Mining requirement for that rock; players with 50 Mining, for example, will not receive [[Mithril ore|mithril]], [[Adamantite ore|adamantite]], or [[runite ore]]. Using boosts will allow players to receive ores they usually can't obtain.

When the sack holds 108 pay-dirt (or 189 if the sack has been upgraded), a game message in the chatbox will state {{Mes|Some ore is ready to be collected from the sack. It's getting full.}}, and players will no longer be able to mine pay-dirt or deposit pay-dirt into the hopper until the sack is emptied below 108 (or 189 if the sack has been upgraded).

===Water circuit===
[[File:Motherlode Mine - Fixing the water wheel.png|thumb|A player using a hammer to fix a waterwheel.]]
At the centre of the mine is a water circuit that connects the [[Hopper (Motherlode Mine)|hoppers]] to a [[Sack (Motherlode Mine)|sack]].

This water flow can be interrupted when the [[strut]]s that support the two large [[Water wheel (Motherlode Mine)|water wheel]]s occasionally break. When both are broken, any pay-dirt that was making its way to the sack will be frozen in place. You may still deposit pay-dirt into the hopper when the water flow is interrupted, but it will not make its way to the sack until the struts have been repaired.

Repairing the struts requires the use of a [[hammer]] (or [[Imcando  hammer]]), which may be found in three of the crates surrounding the machine (the other three contain bronze pickaxes). This process is world specific, not player specific; meaning the struts will break at the same time for everyone, and repairing it will fix it for everyone.

The progress of your pay-dirt will be saved upon logging out or hopping worlds. While you may choose to hop worlds to find one where the struts are not broken, this may take more time than simply repairing them, and may be considered bad etiquette by other players.

Repairing the struts grants [[Smithing]] [[experience]] equal to 1.5 times the player's Smithing level, which will be rewarded on successfully fixing the strut. Chance of repairing improves with a higher level, with a base chance of 12% to repair each tick at level 1 Smithing, increasing to a 27% chance each tick at level 99.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1510918071019610115|date=5 April 2022|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/97492|archivedate=5 April 2022|quote=Yes, it's based on Smithing. 12% at level 1, 27% at level 99 for each roll.}}

Ores are determined when the pay-dirt is mined, not when cleaning.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/608021782449119232|date=8 June 2015|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/99682|archivedate=1 December 2019|quote=When it is mined. It'd stay as runite even if your level drops before you clean it.}} Thus, players wishing to boost should '''do so while mining, not before cleaning'''. Pay-dirt rolls for each ore in descending order, starting from the top tier you're eligible to get.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/jagexash/status/1539706211561607170|date=22 June 2022|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/102638|archivedate=22 July 2022}} With the [[Falador Elite|Falador Elite diary]], the success chance to receive an ore is increased by ~1%.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1536370067935358978|date=13 June 2022|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/109709|archivedate=22 July 2022}} The number of percentage points added to the rate is ~1% for runite ore; ~2% for adamantite ore; and ~1% for mithril ore.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1486771592210403333|date=27 January 2022|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/102827|archivedate=4 June 2023|quote=About 1% more likely to get runite, 2% more likely to get adamant and 1% more likely to get mithril, roughly. Those increases are *added* to the existing percentage chance of getting the ore.}}

The number of golden nuggets received is limited to 3 per batch of pay-dirt deposited into the hopper. While this limit doesn't cause issues during normal gameplay, seasonal events with boosted rates can cause golden nuggets to be deleted. To avoid this, players can deposit half of their pay-dirt at a time by dropping the other half before depositing.

==Money making==
{{Mmgsection|Motherlode Mine}}

==Rewards==
[[Golden nugget]]s can be obtained by searching the sack after cleaning [[pay-dirt]], with each pay-dirt having a 3.13% chance of being a nugget, regardless of a player's [[Mining]] level. This means that, on average, a player should receive a golden nugget every 32 pay-dirts cleaned. 

Golden nuggets stack, and will be collected all at once when searching the sack. Once obtained, they can be spent by speaking to Prospector Percy, to spend at either his [[Prospector Percy's Nugget Shop|shop]], or for various upgrades inside the Motherlode Mine.

===Reward order===
The [[Prospector helmet]] is required for a hard [[Falador Diary]] task. Players looking to complete the diary may consider purchasing the helmet first. If planning to do more [[Motherlode Mine]] in the future, it may be worth selling the helmet back for 32 nuggets (loss of 8) after completing the task in order to unlock the upper floor upgrades first. The helmet '''cannot''' be sold if purchased through the [[Volcanic Mine]] activity.

The upper floor and hopper unlocks should be prioritised if players plan to do more Motherlode Mine, as these provide the most efficient [[Mining]] experience with less attention required.

Outfit pieces should then be obtained in order of what has the highest bonus per nugget; jacket, legs, helmet, then boots. The [[Varrock armour 4]] may be used in place of a prospectors jacket when the elite [[Varrock Diary]] is completed.

The [[coal bag]] is mainly used for [[Blast Furnace]] smithing, where it greatly affects XP and GP rates for any bars requiring coal. See 
[[Blast Furnace/Strategies]] for a detailed overview.

Purchasing the [[gem bag]] along with an equipped and '''charged''' [[amulet of glory]] will maximise gem collection without affecting experience rates. 

The [[Sack (Motherlode Mine)|sack]] capacity upgrade may be purchased last, as the increased experience rates from an additional three deposits per inventory will be negligible compared to the upper level and prospector kit, and 200 [[golden nuggets]] is significantly more expensive.

Players who wish to unlock the upper level will, on average, need to mine from level 30 to level 68, in order to receive enough golden nuggets for the full outfit and the upper level fee. On average, players will need to mine 17,519 pay-dirt to unlock the upper level, upgraded bag, and complete Prospector's kit.

==Experience and efficiency==
The experience and profit rates of Motherlode Mine can vary greatly based on level, the tier of pickaxe used, the amount of other players mining, and whether the upper floor is used.

Compared to other methods, Motherlode Mine requires significantly lower effort, while still offering moderate experience and profit. Mining [[iron ore]] or [[granite]] provides significantly higher experience rates at the cost of being more click-intensive and offering no profit, as items are dropped when mining.

Due to the ore vein timer starting after the first ore is mined, mining veins on low population worlds that are not in use by other players will provide more consistent timings and require less effort; though it also means that the [[strut]]s are less likely to be repaired by another player, which can be especially inconvenient when using the hopper on the upper level of the mine.

To maximise the capacity of the sack, players should have an inventory with only 1 space occupied by a hammer '''or''' gem/coal bag with an [[Imcando hammer (off-hand)]] equipped. This setup will result with 4 trips (7 trips with the upgraded sack) with a full inventory of pay-dirt before having to empty the sack.

Players can expect the following XP rates, assuming the following unlocks:

* Upper level is unlocked at level 57 [[Mining]].  
* [[Dragon pickaxe]] is used from level 61 Mining.   
* [[Prospector kit|Prospector's outfit]] is worn.   
* The upper floor Super Hopper is unlocked.

==Trivia==
[[File:Rockfall partyhat.png|thumb|Some falling rocks wearing party hats during Christmas.]]
*The rockfalls share the same model as the [[pet rock]] when they fall from the ceiling. As a result, the falling rocks wear party hats during Christmas.
*When a player climbs up the ladder, the player character does not actually move up a plane in the game; rather, the terrain on the upper level is simply raised up from the ground on the plane the player character is standing on, so the player will be able to see other players and NPCs on both levels. This is similar to the mechanics in [[Castle Wars]].
*There are several popular culture and community references within the Motherlode Mine:
**On the western side of the mine, there is an [[NPC]] named [[Runite Minor]], who is named after the designer of the Motherlode Mine and winner of the [[Update:PDC: Brains over brawn winner!|2014 Player Designed Content competition]].
**In the middle of Prospector Percy's machine, there is a baby mole with the examine text "''Mooooooooooooole''", a reference to a scene from the film ''{{WP|Austin Powers in Goldmember}}''.
**Prospector Percy's appearance and examine text are references to the character Stinky Pete from ''{{WP|Toy Story 2}}''.
**The miner in the north-eastern corner of the mine has examine text that reads "''Secretly, he'd like to rescue princesses and eat mushrooms''", a reference to the {{WP|Mario (franchise)|''Mario'' video game franchise}} as the miners share a similar appearance to its titular character.
**A miner in the south-western corner reveals that "he became a miner after his {{WP|agoraphobia}} stopped him doing Sailing", a reference to the [[Sailing]] skill.
**A miner along the east wall's examine text reads "He could have been a great ballet dancer if they'd let him try." This is a reference to the film ''{{WP|Billy Elliot}}'', about a father's expectations for his son to be a miner, and not to follow his dreams of being a dancer.
**A miner on the eastern side has the examine text "professional miners don't actually whistle while they work" which is a reference to Disney's Snow White and the Seven Dwarves
**The name Motherlode Mine itself may be an homage to "MotherLoad" - a popular Flash game involving mining seams of ore, released the same year as RuneScape 2.
*The machine [[Prospector Percy]] built to wash the pay-dirt is a cheap knockoff of the machine used in the [[Lovakengj]] [[blast mine]]. According to the [[operator]]s, the design is a secret, and those who try to copy it would "never get it quite right" and "their machine would break down all the time", referencing the fact that the struts on the water wheel often break.
*If all the ores are collected from 85 to 99 Mining at Motherlode Mine, it will average out to 6,344,981 Smithing experience.
*The In-game levelling guide erroneously claims level 30 mining is required for access, it is only required to mine the paydirt and the area can be accessed at level 1 (allowing you to train smithing on the struts without a mining level)
